description:
crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/backend.rs:92-104:

    fn is_per_user_property(prop: &str) -> bool {
        matches!(
            prop,
            \"keywords\" | \"color\" | \"freeBusyStatus\" | \"useDefaultAlerts\" | \"alerts\"
        )
    }

Three contract issues:

1. STATIC, NOT INSTANCE: the method has no \`&self\` receiver. A consumer who wants to vary per-user-property classification per-account (\"this account is on the per-channel feature flag, treat property X as per-user\") cannot. Once the trait ships, adding a self receiver is a breaking change because every override site needs updating.

2. HARDCODED LIST IN A TRAIT DEFAULT: the default impl bakes in the draft-tasks-06 §4.5.1 list. The draft is not yet RFC; a draft-07 revision that adds, renames, or removes a per-user property requires this crate to ship a new version. Consumers who do not override and stay pinned to a stale crate version silently mis-route patches. The matches!(...) shape also offers no programmatic way for a consumer to ask \"what is the canonical list\" without re-reading the source.

3. DIVERGES FROM CANONICAL SIBLING SHAPE: the calendars-server equivalent is structured as a FREE FUNCTION in the types crate:

    crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/backend.rs:118:
    pub fn is_per_user_calendar_event_property(name: &str) -> bool { ... }

…which has the following advantages over the trait-default-method shape:

    - Single source of truth lives next to the type definition.
    - Backends do not have to override (cannot accidentally diverge from spec).
    - Caller code can use it directly without a trait import / generic bound.
    - Type-crate evolution is independent of server-crate evolution.

The calendars-types pattern is what the workspace canonical-template (jmap-mail-types / jmap-mail-server) shape would predict for new properties as well. This is a divergence in the tasks crate that the propagation-rule sweep should converge.

Additionally — and this is the contract footgun — the handler routing at task.rs:255-261 uses B::is_per_user_property(k) to decide whether to call update_task_per_user OR update_object. If a consumer overrides is_per_user_property to add a vendor property but forgets to extend update_task_per_user to handle it (or vice versa), the backend silently does the wrong thing. The two contract surfaces are not type-system-linked.

Recommended convergence (matches sibling calendars):

  - Move classification to jmap-tasks-types as a pub free fn is_per_user_task_property(name: &str) -> bool.
  - Remove the trait default method.
  - Handler calls the free fn directly.
  - Backends that need vendor-extension per-user classification add a sibling fn AND override update_task_per_user — both opt-ins, both visible to type-system review.
title: TasksBackend::is_per_user_property is a static method with hardcoded 5-property list — diverges from sibling calendars (free fn in types crate), cannot evolve per-account, breaks symmetry with update_task_per_user routing
